extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, chymists, and learned readers evaluating chymical theory and experiments (early modern chemistry)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical evaluation of chymists' claims about the principles/elements obtained by distillation (salt, sulphur, mercury/spirit), the adequacy of experimental procedures, and the coherence of their terminology and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purity/simplicity requirement for 'elements' obtained by distillation
rubrics_metrics.description: Those distinct Substances which Chymists are wont to obtain from Mixt Bodies, by their Vulgar Destillation, are not pure and simple enough to deserve, in Rigour of speaking, the Name of Elements, or Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/argument: The author insists that products of common distillation must be shown to be ‘exquisite[ly] simple’ before being called elemental. Many distillates contain mixtures (magisteries, salts, resinous or saline parts) and thus experimentalists must demonstrate true simplicity/purity (not merely a superficial resemblance) before assigning the name of Element or Principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for experimental demonstration before belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Because such promises are wont ... to be much more easily made, then made good by Chymists, I must withhold my Beliefe from their assertions, till their Experiments exact it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/expectation: Extraordinary claims (e.g., reduction to elementary simplicity by further purification, fixing mercuries into gold) require precise, reproducible experiments; assertions without exact experimental proof should not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inferring elemental identity from single general qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: It is somewhat a gross Way of judging of the Nature of Bodies, to conclude without Scruple, that those must be of the same Nature that agree in some such General Quality, as Fluidity, Dryness, Volatility, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: Shared macroscopic states (volatility, fixity, flammability, taste) can encompass many very different substances. Evaluators should require multiple, discriminating properties rather than a single shared quality to claim two things are the same elemental kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminological clarity and prohibition of 'abuse of words'
rubrics_metrics.description: the Chymists do as well in this case, as in many others, allow themselves a License to abuse Words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Definitions must be clear, non-metaphorical, and consistent. The text criticises encomiac or enigmatic descriptions (e.g., Beguinus' & Quercetanus' descriptions of Mercurius) and demands precise explication rather than poetic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency between definitions and doctrinal assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: If Mercury be an Acid Liquor, either Hermetical Philosophy must err in ascribing all Tasts to Salt, or else Mercury must not be a Principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Theories must be self-consistent — properties assigned to a named principle (e.g., taste assigned to salt) must not contradict descriptive claims made elsewhere about that principle. Contradictory attributions in the doctrine undermine its credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for contamination and the role of reagents/assistants in separations
rubrics_metrics.description: the processes of separation I find in Authors ... are to be performed by the assistance of other bodies, so hardly, if upon any termes at all, separable from them, that it is very difficult to give the separated principles all their due, and no more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: When claiming to isolate principles, practitioners must show the separation is not due to reagents or introduced auxiliaries; they must account for and eliminate artefacts/contaminants introduced by the methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversibility and capture of dissipated parts as proof of elemental identity
rubrics_metrics.description: If it should be Objected, that the Dissipated Parts of this flaming Oyle may be caught and collected again into Oyl or Sulphur; I shall demand, what Chymist appears to have ever done it;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Where a process (e.g., combustion) is claimed to reveal elemental identity, there should be a demonstration of reversibility or of reassembling the dissipated part into the original substance — otherwise the inference is weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑generalisability / requirement of cross‑kingdom applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: this quinary number of Elements ... ought at least to have been restrain'd to the Generality of Animal and Vegetable Bodies ... in the Mineral Kingdom, there is scarce one Concrete that has been evinc'd to be adequately divisible into such five Principles or Elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: A proposed universal schema (e.g., three or five principles) must be shown to apply across minerals, vegetables, and animals. Lack of applicability to one kingdom (especially minerals) weakens claims of universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise that supposed 'principles' may be secondary or composite
rubrics_metrics.description: those Principles whereinto Minerals are immediately resolved, which Chymists with great ostentation shew us as the true principles, of them, are but Secundary Principles, or Mixts of a peculiar sort, which must be themselves reduc'd to a very differing forme, to be of the same kind with Vegetable and Animal Liquors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Treat putative principles as potentially composite; demand further analysis to ascertain whether they are truly primitive or themselves mixtures that can be decomposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer experiment over speculative_reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: I declar'd to him ... that I would not engage my self at present to do any more then examine the usual proofs alledg'd by Chymists, for the Vulgar doctrine of their three Hypostatical Principles; You will easily perceive that I am not oblig'd to make answer to what you newly propos'd
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Critique should focus on demonstrative proofs/experiments rather than speculative, a priori reasons. Speculative theories are insufficient without empirical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish heterogeneity within named categories
rubrics_metrics.description: it may be doubted whether or no those earths are all of them perfectly alike
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Categories such as 'earth', 'phlegme', 'spirit' may encompass heterogenous substances; practitioners should not treat members of a category as uniform without justification and should test for internal differences (e.g., different 'earths' or 'spirits').

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical/medicinal efficacy as diagnostic evidence (but not sole proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Phlegme of Vitriol (for instance) is a very effectual remedie against burnes; and I know a very Famous and experienc'd Physitian, whose unsuspected secret ... for the discussing of hard and Obstinate Tumours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Observable, repeatable practical effects (medical efficacy, dissolution behaviours with reagents) provide useful evidence about a substance's properties. However, such efficacy should be integrated with chemical analysis rather than taken alone as proof of elemental nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge species‑specific variants of supposed elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sulphur aliud in auro, aliud in argento, aliud in ferro ... Item aliud in lapidibus, silice, salibus, fontibus, &c. nec vero tot sulphura tantum, sed & totidem salia; ... Alius in Metallis, alius in Gemmis, &c. Ita ut unicuique speciei suus peculiaris Mercurius sit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: The same nominal 'principle' (sulphur, salt, mercury) may occur in distinct forms specific to particular metals, gems, or natural kinds; claims of uniformity must account for such variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware that changes of texture/motion can create new qualities without new ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: a portion of matter may without being Compounded with new Ingredients, by having the Texture and Motion of its small parts chang'd, be easily, by the means of the Fire, endow'd with new Qualities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Experimenters should consider that novel behaviours (e.g., inflammability, colour) may arise from physical reconfiguration rather than from uncovering pre‑existing simple elements; thus inferential caution is required when assigning ontological status to observed changes.
